statement: A commuting family on a finite-dimensional vector space has a simultaneous eigenbasis after a splitting-field extension if one member has distinct eigenvalues. More precisely, let R be henselian local, M finite free of rank d, and A belong to a commuting family in End_R(M). If the characteristic polynomial of A modulo the maximal ideal is separable of degree d, then after a finite étale local extension R′ splitting its residue polynomial the module is a direct sum of rank-one common eigenspaces. For a complete DVR, this yields compatible bases modulo every power of its uniformizer. The splitting extension, a specified finite free module and commuting lifted operators are necessary hypotheses; this does not construct the modular-form module or its integral Hecke operators.
